name: Production Readiness Decision
promise: Decide whether one frozen physical-product configuration can support one named production commitment.
summary: A frozen configuration, commitment-specific DFM and pilot evidence, only the production modules that actually apply, and an independently challenged ready, repair-required, or no-go receipt.
useWhen: A measured prototype faces a concrete quantity, quality, cost, schedule, or delivery commitment.
A pilot or supplier decision needs evidence tied to one frozen configuration.
notFor: Early concept exploration or first functional proof.
Universal production planning before a production commitment exists.
Launching, funding, or selling the product.

workstreams.name: Frozen configuration and commitment
workstreams.brief: Freeze one revision and define volume, cost, quality, schedule, delivery, claims, and change-control boundaries.

workstreams.name: DFM and representative pilot
workstreams.brief: Produce commitment-specific DFM, process, test, yield, rework, and pilot evidence plus only active modules.

workstreams.name: Independent production challenge
workstreams.brief: Challenge assumptions, normalize evidence, expose unpriced or untested risks, and decide without turning plans into proof.

guardrails: Do not infer production readiness from prototype success, documents, quotes, or simulations alone.
Do not contact suppliers, buy parts, fabricate, certify, or commit spend without separate approval.
Do not activate compliance, logistics, firmware, or service work when the product architecture and commitment do not require it.
Preserve supplier confidentiality, quote assumptions, revision identity, and measurement uncertainty.
Ready applies only to the frozen configuration and named commitment; it is not authorization to spend, order, certify, sell, or scale.
verification: Verify the frozen revision and change-control boundary.
Recompute cost, yield, capacity, and schedule claims from preserved evidence.
Challenge the representative pilot against the named commitment.
Fail or require repair for every applicable unproven critical claim.
Confirm the prerequisite baseline before beginning work: A representative functional prototype has passed its measured contract.
Freeze one candidate and one production commitment before collecting evidence.
Complete only the DFM and representative pilot work needed to test that commitment.
Activate modules from architecture, market, and promise evidence—not generic checklists.
Have an independent reviewer challenge denominators, representativeness, economics, and missing proof.

expectations.statement: One production candidate and its allowed changes are unambiguous.
The production decision is tied to a named quantity, quality, cost, schedule, and delivery boundary.
Manufacturing processes and critical interfaces are supported by direct DFM evidence.
A representative pilot supports the named commitment and records yield, defects, rework, and limits.
Supplier feasibility and normalized economics support the commitment. Applicable when: External supplier capacity, pricing, tooling, MOQ, or lead time determines the commitment.
Electrical production testing detects named assembly faults. Applicable when: The product contains production electronics requiring assembly fault detection.
Firmware identity, flashing, keys, and recovery are controlled. Applicable when: Units require firmware, configuration, credentials, or field recovery.
Applicable market-access obligations and evidence gaps are explicit. Applicable when: The named market or product claims create regulatory or certification obligations.
Named reliability risks have representative test evidence. Applicable when: The commitment includes life, duty-cycle, environmental, or warranty exposure.
Packaging and logistics evidence covers the named delivery commitment. Applicable when: The commitment includes physical shipment or storage.
Required service, repair, and replacement paths are feasible. Applicable when: The commitment includes warranty, repair, replacement, or field service.
A representative functional prototype has passed its measured contract.
failureModes: baseline does not match the proposed work

expectations.statement: Production readiness decision produces enough evidence for an independent readiness decision. The possible decisions are ready, repair-required, no-go. Ready applies only to the frozen configuration and named commitment; it is not authorization to spend, order, certify, sell, or scale.
failureModes: missing evidence for the declared outcome
decision made from assumptions or unverified claims
